title: Perpetual reduction for the \(\lambda\sigma\) calculus
formal: Editorial precise variant: does the untyped basic \(\lambda\sigma\) rewrite system specified below admit a total computable one-step strategy which follows an infinite reduction from every term that admits any infinite reduction?
definitions:
Terms and substitutions are finite syntax trees generated by \(a,b ::= 1\mid ab\mid\lambda a\mid a[s]\) and \(s,t ::= \mathrm{id}\mid\uparrow\mid a\mathbin{\cdot}s\mid s\circ t\). The symbol 1 is the first de Bruijn index; other indices can be represented using shifts. There are no additional metavariable constructors or typing restrictions.

One-step reduction is the closure under all well-sorted term and substitution contexts, including under lambda and inside substitutions, of precisely these rules:\[\begin{aligned}(\lambda a)b&\to a[b\cdot\mathrm{id}],&1[\mathrm{id}]&\to1,\\1[a\cdot s]&\to a,&(ab)[s]&\to a[s]b[s],\\(\lambda a)[s]&\to\lambda(a[1\cdot(s\circ\uparrow)]),&a[s][t]&\to a[s\circ t],\\\mathrm{id}\circ s&\to s,&\uparrow\circ\mathrm{id}&\to\uparrow,\\\uparrow\circ(a\cdot s)&\to s,&(a\cdot s)\circ t&\to a[t]\cdot(s\circ t),\\(s\circ t)\circ u&\to s\circ(t\circ u).\end{aligned}\]These are the basic system of §3.1 of the original paper, rather than its later extensions by extra rules. Composition orientation is fixed by the closure rule.

A strategy is a total Turing-computable function on finite terms that returns either one immediate reduct or a halt marker. It returns halt exactly on irreducible terms. Iteration must be infinite whenever any infinite sequence of these rewrite steps starts at the input. If every reduction from a term is finite, strategy iteration must consequently end in a normal form. No oracle for strong normalization, lookahead oracle or time bound is allowed. The effective one-step requirement and the choice of the basic rule set explicitly sharpen the source’s broad strategy question.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked computable strategy with legality, totality and perpetuality proofs, or prove that none exists for exactly this system. A strategy for a different explicit-substitution calculus, or a definition that branches on undecidable strong normalization, is insufficient.
context:
The basic system makes substitution operations part of the syntax. Its complete rewrite rules are fixed here to avoid conflating different extensions.

Kesner explains that the perpetuality argument for the safe-composition calculus does not cover lambda-sigma and leaves a strategy question for it.
why: A perpetual strategy would expose nontermination in a foundational calculus of explicit substitution.

import_provenance.original_title: A perpetual reduction strategy for the λσ calculus
import_provenance.original_statement: Construct an effective perpetual reduction strategy for the full λσ explicit-substitution calculus: whenever a term admits an infinite reduction, the strategy must itself produce an infinite reduction. Kesner explicitly identifies this problem in studying safe and fully compositional substitution calculi.

sentences: Substitutions are explicit syntax and may themselves be reduced.
The card lists the complete basic untyped rewrite system.

Whenever any infinite reduction exists, its own reduction must also be infinite.
